name: Software engineering: pairwise covering array for an industrial healthcare model
description: Build a smallest pairwise covering array for the 35-parameter Healthcare4 model, one of the IBM industrial combinatorial test design models of Segall et al., under its forbidden value combinations. Every feasible pair of values must appear in some test; fewer tests is better.

sources.locator: Segall, Tzoref-Brill and Farchi (ISSTA 2011): combinatorial test design with binary decision diagrams; source of the 20 IBM industrial models, including Healthcare4.
Jia, Cohen, Harman and Petke (ICSE 2015): hyperheuristic search for constrained covering arrays; publishes the benchmark archive used here.
ICSE15_HHSA_Benchmarks.zip (CC BY 4.0): CASA-format model and constraint files; levels are numbered from 1.
Supplementary table of the FastCA repository: HHSA and CASA sizes (2-way and 3-way, 5-hour cutoff) on the same HHSA-format instance files.

requirements.datasets: One CASA model from the ICSE 2015 CIT benchmark archive (Zenodo 581657, CC BY 4.0), prepared by scripts/prepare_software.py.

evaluation.benchmark: Software engineering: pairwise covering array for an industrial healthcare model
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: generate(model) -> list of rows. model = {'name': str, 'strength': t, 'values': [v_0, ..., v_{k-1}], 'forbidden': [[[p, level], ...], ...]}: parameter p takes a level in 0..v_p-1 and each forbidden entry lists parameter-level pairs that must not all occur in one row. Return a list of rows, each a list of k Python ints. Every row must avoid all forbidden combinations, and the rows together must contain every combination of levels of t distinct parameters that occurs in at least one valid configuration (the evaluator decides feasibility exactly). Score: number of rows, minimised; an array that misses a feasible combination or contains a forbidden one is invalid. generate() runs in a sandboxed subprocess (no files, network or subprocesses; CPU limit 60 s for pairwise and 120 s for 3-way tasks, 2 GB); it should be deterministic (seed any randomness, do not read clocks).

limitations: Published sizes on these exact files: HHSA and CASA 46 rows (FastCA repository supplementary table, 5-hour cutoff); the counting lower bound is 42.
The array size is the only objective; generation time is bounded by the sandbox CPU limit and is not scored, whereas the published solvers ran for 1000 s to 5 h in C++.
Feasible combinations are decided by an exact search at preparation time and cross-checked with Z3 in the tests; a Z3 disagreement would change the required set.
The models are public; a candidate could embed a precomputed array. Scores are comparable with published sizes only for arrays generated within the contract.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Combinatorial interaction testing of configurable software: choose as few test configurations as possible such that every feasible combination of t option settings is exercised, while respecting constraints that forbid some option combinations.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Configurable systems such as compilers, web servers and model checkers have astronomically many configurations; interaction faults are triggered by a few options together, so smaller constrained covering arrays reduce testing cost while keeping the interaction coverage guarantee. Constraint handling is a central open difficulty because invalid configurations cannot be executed.
